subject: GPU pool thresholds and eviction policy review for private deployment
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Subject: [Action] GPU pool thresholds and eviction policy review for private deployment

Hi Liam / Priya —

Thanks again for the walkthrough of your VPC setup yesterday. As we move from discovery toward a staged rollout, the engineering team needs to agree on concrete thresholds and eviction behavior for the private GPU pool so our autoscaler and cache subsystem behave predictably. Im attaching a lightweight capacity model (capacity_model_v3.xlsx) and a sample of observed p99 response latencies from our hosted traces (response_latency_samples.csv).

Key asks:
- Proposed sustained throughput target: 4.5k tokens/sec (aggregate) for the initial commit; confirm this aligns with your expected traffic floor.
- Scale-up trigger: sustained 75% GPU util for 30s across the pool OR average queue depth > 180 requests for 60s.
- Scale-down trigger: sustained < 45% GPU util for 2m and queue depth < 40.
- Eviction policy for in-memory KV/prefix cache: LRU with a soft TTL for keys older than 20m; on eviction spikes prefer evicting largest-value keys first to preserve short-context hot paths.
- Graceful degradation: when capacity hits 95% for >2m, route best-effort requests to a lower-cost quantized variant (q4f) with a per-request header X-Redwood-Fallback: q4f.

Questions for you:
1) Any networking egress/ingress shaping on your side we should account for (burst throttles, policing)?
2) Does your ops team want to control the scale-up ramp (fixed N GPU per step) or rely on percent-of-pool adjustments?
3) Are the proposed TTL/eviction knobs compatible with your memory accounting on the on-prem nodes?

Next steps: If this looks reasonable, Id like to schedule a 60m dry-run next week with a synthetic spike to validate warm-pool behavior and eviction churn. Proposed slots: Tue 14 Sep or Thu 16 Sep, mornings PT.

Thanks —
Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior PM, Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity_model_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), response_latency_samples.csv (csv)

Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Action] GPU pool thresholds and eviction policy review for private deployment

Mina —

Appreciate the detailed ask and the attachments. Quick answers from ops perspective:

- Network shaping: our cloud edge enforces an egress policer at application layer that limits sustained bursts above 2Gbps for a single /24; short spikes (under 60s) are allowed but anything sustained will be throttled. We'll share the exact policer config as part of the dry-run pack.
- Scaling ramp: we prefer fixed-step ramps (add 2 GPUs per scale-up step) to keep migration and GPU warmup predictable. Percent-of-pool leads to noisy rebalances with our heterogenous cores.
- Memory accounting: nodes are configured with a memory guard at 88% host memory. Eviction based on largest-value-first+sized LRU is fine, but we will need an explicit cap on per-model KV allocation to avoid noisy neighbor effects.

On sustained throughput: 4.5k tokens/sec seems fine for the first tranche provided we have a hard upper bounding QPS gate at the edge to prevent sudden on-ramp; otherwise, well see queue buildup.

We can do the dry-run Tue 14 Sep 10:00 PT. Priya, can you confirm ops runbook availability?

—Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Ops, Stratus AI

Thanks Liam — couple of engineering notes inline: 

- Fixed-step ramps (add 2 GPUs) is OK, we'll wire that into the autoscaler. We will implement a cooldown window per-step of 180s to allow KV warm-up to settle.
- For the queue depth thresholds: our admission controller measures active requests as requests with a pinned session in the scheduler; the thresholds Mina suggested map to roughly 1.8k concurrent tokens in flight in our microbench. If Stratus can implement the edge QPS gate, we'll avoid spike-induced thundering.
- Eviction: we will expose two knobs via the runtime config: per-model-kv-cap (bytes), and eviction-batch-size. We propose default per-model-kv-cap=1.2GB and eviction-batch-size=64 entries. If host memory guard hits 92%, we will trigger aggressive compaction (reduce per-model-kv-cap by 20% for 5m).

Ive updated the capacity_model_v3.xlsx with an autoscale step simulation (tab: autoscale-v2). I will push a cleaned PDF to the Drive link tonight.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Thanks — confirmed. Ops will provide the policer map and the test harness for the dry-run. A couple of small clarifications from our side: 

1) We will run the first dry-run against a staging pool sized to our expected initial commit: 6x A100-like nodes (heterogeneous generation) matching your 4.5k tokens/sec target. If the warmup path requires additional GPUs we will coordinate a second staged run.
2) For the fallback plan (q4f), we need the runtime to emit a diagnostic header indicating which tokens were served from fallback and the model variant used (header: X-Redwood-Model-Variant). This will help our QA and SRE correlate quality delta versus latency improvements.

We are good for Tue 14 Sep 10:00 PT. Attaching the runbook stub: network_diagram_vpc2.png

Perfect — thanks everyone for the quick responses and the confirmations. Summary and short plan: 

- Confirmed targets: 4.5k tokens/sec sustained floor; fixed-step ramp +2 GPUs per step; dry-run Tue 14 Sep 10:00 PT against 6-node staging pool.
- Runtime knobs: per-model-kv-cap=1.2GB default, eviction-batch-size=64, aggressive compaction at 92% host memory.
- Network constraints: Stratus to provide policer map (2Gbps sustained per /24) and an edge QPS gate for the test.
- Observability: runtime to emit X-Redwood-Fallback and X-Redwood-Model-Variant headers; Redwood will also capture token-level fallback counts and produce a 30m post-run report.

- Jonas: drop the autoscale-pdf to Drive and paste the link in this thread (ETA EOD 11 Sep).
